amendments.normalized_body: In `shrimp.rs` line 554, the `critical_gh_deficit` check `(gh_d / params.gh_min_d.max(0.01)) < params.critical_molt_gh_ratio` does not guard against `gh_min_d = 0.0` the same way `molt_mineral_modifier` does. When a user sets `gh_min_d = 0.0` (semantically 'no GH minimum'), the `.max(0.01)` guard converts it to 0.01, causing any GH below `0.01 * critical_molt_gh_ratio = 0.003` to falsely trigger a critical deficit override. The fix is to add a check: `let critical_gh_deficit = params.gh_min_d > 0.0 && (gh_d / params.gh_min_d.max(0.01)) < params.critical_molt_gh_ratio;`. The existing test `test_zero_ca_and_mg_min_parameters_use_defensive_guards` (line 411) does not check `last_molt_success` and misses this edge case — it should assert that molt succeeds when all minimums are disabled.

In `update_molt_stress` (shrimp.rs lines 498-504), the `thermal_stress` component only tracks temperatures above `optimal_temp_max_c`. Cold temperatures (below `optimal_temp_min_c`) contribute zero thermal_stress to `molt_stress_index`, even though they reduce molt success via `thermal_factor` in `molt_cycle`. This means chronic cold exposure does not build up molt stress over time — it only causes individual molt failures when they resolve, which then indirectly raise stress via `failed_molt_accum`. Consider adding a symmetric cold-temperature branch: `if temp < optimal_temp_min_c { ((optimal_temp_min_c - temp) / temp_condition_low_divisor_c).clamp(0.0, molt_stress_thermal_cap) }` to match the heat stress path.

crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:555-556 still hardcodes `let temp_factor = raw_temp_factor.max(0.25);` inside `molt_cycle`, even though crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1611-1620 and crates/tank_data/data/shrimp/neocaridina_davidi.toml:164-171 now make the temperature floor species-configurable via `temp_condition_min_factor`. Any preset value below `0.25` changes condition/success scoring but has no effect on molt cadence, so the new parameter is only partially effective and the model still hides a thermal timing constant. Either parameterize the cadence floor separately or use the named floor consistently when computing `effective_interval`.

Validation for `temp_condition_min_factor` disagrees across data entry paths: crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:981-1005 rejects `0.0` by treating the field as strictly positive, while crates/tank_core/src/invariants.rs:466-469 accepts `0.0` with `check_unit_interval`. As a result, a runtime/save-state configuration can legally use `0.0`, but the equivalent species preset cannot be authored or round-tripped through the preset layer. Align the lower bound across preset validation, runtime invariants, and tests/docs.
